content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through adding jquery through a cdn with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns understanding content delivery networks into a repeatable implementation choice. A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates adding jquery through a cdn using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
